title: Button or API for users to switch between themes
body:
### Problem

As of now (version 1.15.2), for users to switch the theme, they have to go to the hamburger menu to access the setting. This is not very intuitive for the end users if they are not familiar with Streamlit. In addition, if I hide the hamburger menu in my app, the users won't be able to change the theme by themselves at all.

### Solution

It would be nice to have a button outside the hamburger menu for users to quickly switch between light mode and dark mode (or other themes if available). 

Another solution would be to provide an API for switching between the themes, so the developers can implement the theme switcher by themselves if needed.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-5908)

# Update

Hey all! We haven't started working on this but thanks for all the comments and upvotes! I'm not sure if we can move it completely outside of the app menu since then we'd potentially have a lot of controls (especially if deployed on Community Cloud). But I agree having it in the settings dialog is pretty unintuitive. One idea I had was to put a theme switch directly inside of the app menu, similar to the toggles in Notion's page menu below. Thanks! Here a slightly more robust version. Would be great if the streamlit team would provide a non-private access to set_option, at least for ui settings like dark mode.
```
toggle_dark = st.toggle("Dark Layout", value=True)
if st.get_option("theme.base") == "light" and toggle_dark:
    st._config.set_option("theme.base", "dark")  # type: ignore # noqa: SLF001
    st.rerun()
elif st.get_option("theme.base") == "dark" and not toggle_dark:
    st._config.set_option("theme.base", "light")  # type: ignore # noqa: SLF001
    st.rerun()
```

On my local machine this works for me (in Firefox), despite throwing an exception. But when deploying to a server it does not work.
```
streamlit.errors.StreamlitAPIException: theme.base cannot be set on the fly. Set as command line option, e.g. streamlit run script.py --theme.base, or in config.toml instead.
```

Here is the solution provided by [Cursor](https://www.cursor.com/) :)

It involves putting a file `themes.toml` in `.streamlit` folder which has all the themes you want to select from.

```
# Load themes from themes.toml
def load_themes():
    themes_file = os.path.join('.streamlit', 'themes.toml')
    if os.path.exists(themes_file):
        with open(themes_file, 'r') as f:
            themes = toml.load(f)
            return {k.replace('theme.', ''): v for k, v in themes.items()}
    return {}

# Update theme function
def update_theme(theme_dict):
    for key, value in theme_dict.items():
        st._config.set_option(f"theme.{key}", value)  # type: ignore # noqa: SLF001


# Theme selector
themes = load_themes()
theme_names = list(themes.keys())
selected_theme = st.sidebar.selectbox(
    "Select Theme",
    theme_names,
    index=theme_names.index('dark') if 'dark' in theme_names else 0
)

# Apply theme if changed
if 'current_theme' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.current_theme = selected_theme

if selected_theme != st.session_state.current_theme:
    update_theme(themes[selected_theme])
    st.session_state.current_theme = selected_theme
    st.rerun()
```

Yes please - I'd love to have `x` different themes (ex: light / dark / cyber punk) for users to pick from via a select box in the sidebar. 

Trying to do this with css inserts is painful and inconsistent (especially with a chat interface).

Maybe something in the `config.toml` like:
```toml
[theme_x]
<user_inserts_theme>

[theme_y]
<user_inserts_theme>
```

Then the user can call something like
```py
st.select_theme(theme_x)
```

To change between the desired themes.

Would be awesome!
